purpose: Flunisolide is used to help control and prevent symptoms of asthma or to relieve nasal symptoms like stuffiness, runny nose, and sneezing caused by allergies. It helps reduce swelling and irritation in your airways or nasal passages. It is not a rescue inhaler and works best when used regularly every day.
how_it_works: Flunisolide is a steroid that works by calming down inflammation, which is the swelling and irritation in your airways or nose. Think of it like a slow, steady firefighter that keeps the fire of inflammation from flaring up over time. It does not work instantly, but with regular use it makes breathing easier and keeps allergy symptoms under control.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include a sore throat, hoarse voice, cough, or a mild burning or stinging sensation in the nose if using the nasal spray. You may also notice an unpleasant taste or smell. A yeast infection in the mouth called thrush can happen with the inhaler, so always rinse your mouth with water after each use.
warnings: Do not use this medication as a rescue inhaler during a sudden asthma attack — it will not work fast enough. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, especially if you have been using it for a long time. Tell your doctor if you have any infections, as steroids can make it harder for your body to fight them. Long-term use at high doses may affect bone density or slow growth in children, so regular check-ups are important.
typical_dosing: For the asthma inhaler, adults typically take 2 puffs twice a day, morning and evening. For the nasal spray, adults usually use 2 sprays in each nostril twice a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your situation.
